messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — opening a docs PR to convert a few tool-calling examples into the structured-output JSON schema we landed last week. PR is #4127. Need quick eyes from @rachel and @sam :eyes:

rachel: Thanks, Alex. Can you list which snippets change? I can try to batch-review.

alex: Short list: the ecommerce order-cancel flow (old function-calling example), the calendar-invite sample, and the embedding+rerank example that used inline tool calls.

maria: Heads up — the embedding example lives in two pages, docs/embeddings/usage.md and docs/sdk/examples/embeddings.md. We should update both and add a redirect for the old anchor link.

sam: I'll take the calendar snippet. Quick question: are we switching to an "envelope" top-level field (e.g., {"result": {...}}) or flattening the tool output?

alex: We agreed to use an envelope to leave room for metadata and errors: schema looks like:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "result": {"type": "object"},
    "meta": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": true}
  },
  "required": ["result"]
}
```
This avoids breaking callers that expect an outer object.

kevin: For SDK snippets, we also need to show how to parse with the helpers (js/python). I can add a tiny JS helper in sdk/examples/parse.js that does safe parsing + fallback.

rachel: Good. Please include a one-liner about parse fallbacks: if JSON.parse fails, try extracting the first JSON block via regex and retry. Often helps with LLM noise.

alex: I'll add that. Example snippet we can put in the docs:
```js
// safeParse tries to recover a JSON object from noisy text
function safeParse(text) {
  try { return JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) {
    const m = text.match(/\{[\s\S]*\}/);
    return m ? JSON.parse(m[0]) : null;
  }
}
```

maria: Link fixes: the old calendar example URL (docs/flows/calendar.md#tool-calling) is referenced from the migration guide. We should add a permanent redirect and update the migration guide to point to the new example path. I can open a small PR for the redirect config.

sam: Also check the snippet license headers — the embeddings example uses a copied snippet from external lib; legal wants attribution. I'll add a note in the PR description.

kevin: For QA, can we add two tiny unit tests in docs-tests that render the example responses and run safeParse against them? That'll catch obvious formatting regressions.

alex: Yes — I'll add tests and wire them into the docs CI job. Tests can run in headless node with snapshot of example outputs.

docs-bot: Reminder: docs style guide requires "before"/"after" diffs for snippet migrations. Please add inline before/after blocks in the PR description.

rachel: One more thing — examples that call external tools should show explicit guardrails: schema + max_retries + fallback model. Maybe a short checklist at the top of the example page.

maria: I drafted a short checklist in the PR comments: 1) Schema present and validated; 2) Safe parse helper included; 3) Link redirects created; 4) SDK snippet updated; 5) Tests added.

alex: Perfect. I'll update PR #4127 to include that checklist and assign reviewers. Leaving a note to reviewers: prioritize the ecommerce order-cancel flow — customer-facing.

sam: If you want, I can start the ecommerce review now. Ping me when PR is updated.

alex: Will do in 10–15m. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

kevin: After merge, can we add a short entry to the migration guide that lists the new envelope schema and a one-line compatibility note for older callers? I can write that if nobody objects.

rachel: Please do. Keep it under 6 lines.

alex: No objections. Assigning kevin for the migration blurb.

maria: I'll open the redirect PR and link it in #4127.

docs-bot: Deployed preview for PR #4127 available at https://deploy-preview-4127--docs.redwood.ai/docs/tooling/structured-output (expires in 24h).

alex: Nice — will skim the preview and drop fixes. Thanks all.
